name: Hotel Imperial, Vienna
positioning: Hotel Imperial, a Luxury Collection Hotel: a former ducal palace on Vienna's Ringstrasse in the first district, furnished with antiques, marble and chandeliers
best_for: Travelers who want to stay in a historic palace in central Vienna
Guests who value butler and concierge service

facts.text: The hotel is in Vienna's first district, directly on the Ringstrasse (Ring Boulevard).
The building was originally a private palace built for Duke Philipp of Wuerttemberg.
Duke Philipp of Wuerttemberg had the palace built in 1863 as a token of his love for his wife, Archduchess Marie Therese.
Interiors feature marble, hand-carved statues and crystal chandeliers.
The Royal Staircase in the lobby leads up to the rooms and suites beneath chandeliers and high stucco ceilings.
Rooms and suites are appointed with original paintings, antiques, stucco ceilings and fine fabrics.
Rooms are furnished with authentic antiques, silk-covered walls and marble bathrooms.
The Sisi Suites are named after Empress Sisi.
A private butler service is available on request.
Alfred Hitchcock, Charlie Chaplin and Richard Wagner are among the hotel's past guests.
Café Imperial Wien serves Viennese classics such as Tafelspitz, Wiener Schnitzel and the handmade Imperial Torte.
Afternoon tea is served daily in the Imperial Bar.

highlights.text: The Royal Suites were once the private apartments of Prince Philipp of Wuerttemberg, with crystal chandeliers on seven-metre stucco ceilings.
Private balconies offer views over the roofs and spires of old Vienna.
There are three Clefs d'Or concierges on the hotel team.
The Imperial Torte was created to mark the hotel's opening, in honour of Emperor Franz Josef I, and its recipe is still a secret.

considerations.text: Parking is off-site; the concierge recommends nearby underground garages.
There are no electric vehicle charging stations at the hotel.
WhataHotel notes the historic building may have some traditional room configurations.
